Record number of migrants arrive in Spain’s Canary Islands
articles.summary: New EU migration and asylum laws have largely failed to stem flow of migrants to Spain and its territories.
articles.body: Spain has declared a migration emergency in the Canary Islands after the arrival of more than 9,000 people in its Atlantic Ocean territory since the start of November. Spain’s Maritime Rescue Service said it had rescued 1,488 migrants aboard 14 dinghies, also known as pirogues, most of whom arrived on El Hierro in the Canary Islands from West Africa on Saturday. That’s broken the record of 1,461 people rescued six years earlier in November 2020. Spain’s Territorial Policy Minister Angel Victor Torres is visiting ⁠El Hierro on Sunday to discuss the surge in migrant arrivals. Al Jazeera’s Bernard Smith, reporting from El Hierro, said the arrival this year has set a record in the 32 years since statistics have been collected. “There’s been even more arrivals by Sunday afternoon”, Smith said, adding that the new arrivals are processed at the port in El Hierro and taken to a reception centre and sent on to other Canary Islands or to the Spanish mainland. The European Union’s new Pact on Migration and Asylum officially came into force on June 12, 2026, introducing “firm and fair rules” for accepting asylum requests, marking the most sweeping overhaul of EU asylum and border laws in decades. “EU states are under pressure to do more to control migration from Africa and from outside the European Union,” Smith said, adding that the new rules haven’t stopped the flow of migrants to Spain and its enclaves. Last month, Spain deported more than a dozen of the 80,000 people who had entered its North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco over a 48-hour period in late July. At least 100 people died during the mass crossing into the autonomous city, which covers just 18.5 square kilometres (7.1sq miles) and has a population of about 80,000. Most of the migrants arriving in El Hierro depart from West Africa, many leaving from Senegal, with hopes of reaching mainland Europe. But to get there, they risk their lives in small, often overcrowded boats at sea. One boat on Saturday was carrying 240 people, including 12 women and 36 children, authorities said. The International Organization for Migration (IOM) recorded at least 450 deaths on the Western African Atlantic route in the first 10 months of 2026. “It is a treacherous journey,” said Al Jazeera’s Nicolas Haque, reporting from Dakar in Senegal, from where some of the boats depart, adding that favourable weather conditions in the Atlantic Ocean have made departures from the coastlines in Africa much easier in recent years. “So when the weather conditions allow it, the boats go out there,” he said, noting that migrants use “wooden fishing vessels called pirogues” in which up to 100 people are packed in for “a journey that can last one week”.

Iran targets US military base in Bahrain with drone attack
articles.summary: It marks the second attack on the country in three days and comes as the US and Iran remain locked in a stand-off over the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.body: Iran launched a drone attack against a US military base in Bahrain on Sunday, its second attempt to target the country in three days. The country's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it targeted the US air defence radar facility at al-Riffa air base in Bahrain using six drones. Bahrain's military said its air defence systems intercepted and destroyed the Iranian air attacks "before they could achieve their objectives". It comes after Iran fired drones at Bahrain on Friday, its first attack against Gulf countries since September. The US and Iran are locked in a stand-off over the Strait of Hormuz. About a fifth of the world's gas and oil supply usually flows through it but shipping has been restricted since the outbreak of war in February. Iran insists that it should control the strait and has been attacking what it calls "unauthorised" traffic, while the US military is providing protection for tankers shuttling oil through the strait to keep exports flowing from Gulf Arab states. As sirens sounded across Bahrain on Sunday the interior ministry called on citizens to head to their nearest safe location. Bahrain's foreign ministry said: "The Kingdom of Bahrain condemns in the strongest terms the continued brutal Iranian attacks on its territory and holds Iran fully responsible for their consequences." In a statement on the strikes shared by Iran's state broadcaster on Telegram, the IRGC said: "The Strait of Hormuz is closed, and any aggression by the American enemy will be met with an even harsher and more forceful response." Earlier this week, the IRGC claimed that it struck a US early warning radar system in Bahrain on Friday. The US military has denied the claim, stating that the IRGC launched two one-way attack drones towards Bahrain and both were shot down by US forces. It added that there were no injuries or damage. Earlier in the week the US carried out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, US officials told CBS, the BBC's US partner. The officials described the strikes as limited and defensive, and said they were in response to the IRGC firing on a US aircraft. Iranian state news agency Irna reported explosions on Qeshm on Monday. The IRGC did not comment but said its forces had shot down two US MQM-170 drones south of the island and a US MQ-9 drone east of the Strait. The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated a naval blockade of Iranian ports. Iranian negotiators had been discussing with mediators a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US meets seven conditions, reportedly including the lifting of the naval blockade and releasing frozen Iranian assets. However this week Donald Trump said that the US was no longer interested in a deal to end the war with Iran and ordered Vice-President JD Vance, who had been involved in efforts to restart negotiations, to focus on domestic US politics. articles.title: Bahrain Says It Intercepted Iranian Attacks As Tehran Claims Strike On US Base
articles.summary: Bahrain said its air defenses intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks on November 15, after explosions and air raid sirens were reported across the Gulf kingdom and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it had targeted a US military installation.
articles.body: Bahrain said its air defenses intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks on November 15, after explosions and air raid sirens were reported across the Gulf kingdom and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) claimed it had targeted a US military installation. The Bahraini military said its air defenses intercepted several attacks before they reached their targets, accusing Tehran of continuing its "systematic hostile approach" toward the kingdom. Bahrain's Foreign Ministry said the country rejected "turning its territory into an arena for settling scores" and held Iran fully responsible for the attacks and their consequences. Iran's IRGC claimed they had launched six drones targeting a US air defense radar system at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain, according to statements carried by Iranian state media. There was no immediate confirmation from US or Bahraini authorities that the radar installation had been hit. Citing its journalists in Bahrain, the AFP news agency reported that explosions were heard around 4 a.m. local time, followed by another series of blasts around 6:30 a.m. Sirens also sounded and Bahraini authorities issued warnings urging residents to seek shelter without specifying the source of the threat. The Interior Ministry told residents to remain calm, proceed to the nearest safe location, and follow official channels for updates. Bahrain, which hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet, has been among the Gulf countries targeted by Iran during the conflict, which began on February 28 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. The reported attack on November 15 came two days after the IRGC said it had targeted a US early-warning radar facility in Bahrain. The US military said at the time that it had intercepted two Iranian drones targeting the island, reporting no casualties or damage. Bahrain has now been targeted twice in three days, following a lull in attacks. The latest developments come amid diplomatic efforts to end the nearly nine-month conflict, which have not yet produced a breakthrough despite a broader lull in fighting. Iran has restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a key global oil transit route, and launched missile and drone attacks on military and civilian infrastructure across the region. US President Donald Trump has told his senior advisers in recent days that he might refrain from further attacks on Iran if Tehran and Iran-backed Houthi fighters in Yemen avoid new provocations, according to Reuters. Trump has also said the US naval blockade of Iran would remain in place. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia's military said on November 15 it had intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles launched toward Riyadh and three drones in the kingdom's oil-rich Eastern Province. RFE/RL journalists report the news in 24 languages in 18 countries where a free press is banned by the government or not fully established. We provide what many people cannot get locally: uncensored news, responsible discussion, and open debate.

Russian envoy outlines Moscow’s concerns over Switzerland’s OSCE chairmanship
articles.summary: He noted that the Russian and Swiss delegations meet every week and that the Swiss side does not withhold information from Russia, Dmitry Polyansky said
articles.body: VIENNA, November 15. /TASS/. Switzerland maintained regular diplomatic contacts with Russia during its chairmanship of the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), but generally sided with the European Union on key issues, Russia’s Permanent Representative to the OSCE Dmitry Polyansky told TASS. "I have no complaints about the Swiss when it comes to maintaining diplomatic contacts," Polyansky said. He noted that the Russian and Swiss delegations meet every week and that the Swiss side does not withhold information from Russia. However, the envoy described Switzerland’s neutrality as highly conditional, saying that Bern follows an openly pro-Ukrainian policy, even if it cannot be described as explicitly anti-Russian. "I cannot say that our voice goes unheard at the OSCE, that they prevent us from speaking or otherwise restrict us. But when they have to make a choice, they, of course, tend to take a position closer to that of the European Union rather than remain neutral. That is our main complaint," Polyansky said. As an example, Polyansky cited the Swiss chairmanship’s refusal to change the wording of a standing agenda item at OSCE meetings, which describes Russia’s special military operation as military aggression against Ukraine. He said this wording prevents Moscow from fully presenting its position. "They had the authority to make that decision and promised to consider changing the wording. But they ultimately decided that making such a change would send the wrong signal to Russia and suggest that they were abandoning their policy of solidarity with Brussels," the Russian envoy said. "How should we interpret this? Could they have changed it? Of course. Did they want to? Clearly, they did not.".

articles.title: The Constitutional Court will resume hearings tomorrow on Georgian Dream’s lawsuit seeking to ban five opposition parties
articles.summary: The Constitutional Court will resume hearings on November 16 regarding Georgian Dream’s lawsuit seeking to ban five opposition political parties. For reference, proceedings on the lawsuit began at the Constitutional Court on October 21.
articles.body: The Constitutional Court will resume hearings on November 16 regarding Georgian Dream’s lawsuit seeking to ban five opposition political parties. For reference, proceedings on the lawsuit began at the Constitutional Court on October 21. The case is being heard by the Plenum of the Constitutional Court, consisting of seven judges. The lawsuit submitted to the Constitutional Court is signed by 88 members of parliament. Based on their petition, the Court is considering declaring the following five political parties unconstitutional: The constitutional lawsuit is accompanied by the findings of the temporary investigative commission established in the 11th convocation of Parliament.

articles.title: Ukraine war briefing: US proposes Kyiv cede land to Russia for Nato membership, Zelenskyy says
articles.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said the US has asked for the first time if Ukraine would withdraw from parts of the eastern Donbas region that Russia does not control in exchange for Ukraine becoming a Nato member . But the Ukrainian president said his country would not surrender territory.
articles.body: Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said the US has asked for the first time if Ukraine would withdraw from parts of the eastern Donbas region that Russia does not control in exchange for Ukraine becoming a Nato member . But the Ukrainian president said his country would not surrender territory. “The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’,” he said in remarks to reporters released by his office on Saturday. “That is why ⁠I believe Nato is back on the agenda.” But he said the suggestion, which would form part of a new postwar security framework for Europe, could allow Russia to weaken Nato and reshape borders. “This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations,” Zelenskyy said. Zelenskyy reiterated his position that Kyiv was not ready to concede territory but said that if it received a comprehensive package including security guarantees, the right to a strong and well-funded ​Ukrainian army and funds to rebuild, he would put the question to a ‌national referendum. Echoing comments ‌made by European leaders at a summit in Dublin on Friday, Zelenskyy dismissed Russia’s call for a broad agreement on European security architecture to be reached before the specifics are ‌agreed on how to end the war in Ukraine. “We cannot turn everything upside down and start by talking about changing the security framework in the world or across the continent overall, and only then talk about ending this war. This war must be ended first,” he said. The Ukrainian president has also rejected the possibility of Ukraine committing to neutrality , something that could only happen if the country’s constitution was changed. “If Putin expects Ukraine’s neutrality to be enshrined, that’s not going to happen,” he said. “We’re not in Nato right now anyway.” US President ⁠Donald Trump’s ⁠envoy and ​son-in-law Jared ⁠Kushner said on ⁠Saturday ​the US ‌was ‌focused on ‌facilitating direct engagement between Russia and ‌European nations on ​the Ukraine war , ⁠after trilateral meetings ​involving Washington, ​Moscow ​and ​Kyiv ‌this ​week. However, Washington and Nato have not yet commented on the suggestion of a swap of the Donbas for Ukraine Nato membership. Negotiations did, however, lead to agreements that European countries would join future talks on ending the war. Zelenskyy has accused SpaceX of not telling the truth over restrictions to Ukraine’s Starshield satellite system , saying the decision to impose speed limits appears to be “political” rather than “technical”. Speaking on Friday, Ukraine’s president said the restrictions affecting Ukrainian drones, in place for five days, meant they could no longer intercept incoming jet-powered Russian Shahed drones. Ukraine suspects the slowdown is a deliberate US tactic, designed to put pressure on Zelenskyy to make concessions to Putin. French President Emmanuel Macron said Saturday that countries seeking to limit aid to Ukraine want to impose an “unjust peace” and warned that it was a recipe for another war . “Those who want to ration aid to Ukraine wish underneath it all to force an unjust peace on it” and, by extension, all of Europe, Macron said on social media. “That is a recipe for another war. That cannot be France’s position.” Russian forces ⁠struck a cargo vessel in ⁠the ⁠Ukrainian ​port of Chornomorsk , RIA ⁠news agency cited the Russian ⁠defence ministry ​as ‌saying on ‌Saturday. The ministry ‌said the ship was being used to supply the Ukrainian ‌military. Meanwhile, Ukrainian strikes on the Samara oil pipeline station near the village of Prosvet in Russia’s Samara region on Friday set several oil storage tanks on fire, Ukraine’s General Staff said. The facility is a key part of the network exporting Russian oil to global markets, the General Staff said. Separately, 22 people were injured in a Russian attack on the south-east Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia on Friday, Ukraine’s Emergency Service said.

articles.summary: BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 15. An ammunition explosion occurred on November 15 in the Jeyranchol area of Azerbaijan's Aghstafa district.
articles.body: BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 15. An ammunition explosion occurred on November 15 in the Jeyranchol area of Azerbaijan's Aghstafa district. The information was confirmed in a joint statement by the press services of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the Prosecutor General's Office, and the Azerbaijan Mine Action Agency (ANAMA). According to the information, the explosion occurred as a result of Rasul Shahin oglu Ibrahimov, born in 1986 and a resident of Demirchilar village in the Gazakh district, and Sahib Amrahov, born in 1982 and a resident of Dash Salahli village in the Gazakh district, handling unexploded ordnance. It was noted that Rasul Ibrahimov died from his injuries, while Sahib Amrahov was injured. ANAMA, the Ministry of Internal Affairs, and the Prosecutor General's Office once again urged citizens to observe safety rules, avoid touching suspicious objects, and refrain from handling explosive ordnance.

articles.title: 7 criminals killed, over 3 tonnes of drugs seized in Egypt police raids
articles.summary: Seven highly dangerous criminals were killed and over three tonnes of drugs were seized during police raids in three Egyptian provinces, the Egyptian Interior Ministry said Saturday, Xinhua reports. The seven killed had previously been convicted of crimes including murder, drug and firearms trafficking, armed robbery, kidnapping and resisting authorities, with sentences ranging up to life imprisonment, the ministry said in a statement.
articles.body: Seven highly dangerous criminals were killed and over three tonnes of drugs were seized during police raids in three Egyptian provinces, the Egyptian Interior Ministry said Saturday, Xinhua reports. The seven killed had previously been convicted of crimes including murder, drug and firearms trafficking, armed robbery, kidnapping and resisting authorities, with sentences ranging up to life imprisonment, the ministry said in a statement. Investigations found criminal groups involving highly dangerous individuals were bringing in quantities of drugs, unlicensed firearms and ammunition for trafficking in several provinces. Following legal procedures, security forces targeted the groups in the Nile Delta provinces of Sharkia, Gharbia and Dakahlia, killing seven criminals and arresting the remaining members, the statement said. Police seized more than three tonnes of various drugs, nearly 150,000 narcotic pills, 115 firearms and a large quantity of ammunition, it added.

Tsikhanouskaya ally condemns Belarusian athlete for insulting Ukrainian opponent, complacency in Russia's war
articles.summary: Pavel Latushka, deputy head of the cabinet of exiled Belarusian opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, on Nov. 14, condemned Belarusian tennis player Aryna Sabalenka for insulting her Ukrainian opponent and not condemning Russia's war. "Absolutely unacceptable behaviour by Belarusian tennis player Aryna Sabalenka!
articles.body: Pavel Latushka, deputy head of the cabinet of exiled Belarusian opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, on Nov. 14, condemned Belarusian tennis player Aryna Sabalenka for insulting her Ukrainian opponent and not condemning Russia's war. "Absolutely unacceptable behaviour by Belarusian tennis player Aryna Sabalenka! Aryna has failed to condemn the aggressive war against Ukraine, the mass repression of Belarusians, has not spoken out in support of the release of political prisoners, not even women, and now she is insulting (Ukrainian Elina Svitolina), against whom a war of annihilation is being waged," he wrote . Sabalenka and Ukrainian tennis player Elina Svitolina faced each other at the women's pro tennis WTA finals in California on Nov. 13, resulting in Svitolina securing a victory against her Belarusian opponent. Reports circulated on social media alleging that Sabalenka muttered insults against Ukrainians or against Ukraine's Svitolina. Latushka reposted the footage of Sabalenka alongside his written post on the social media platform X. "She should be banned from all WTA-sanctioned tournaments... This is the only proportionate response to such behaviour. She is a disgrace to the Belarusian people," Latushka said. Russia and Belarus have faced bans in various international sports bodies for Russia's war against Ukraine. Despite the Kremlin's ties with many Russian athletes, Moscow and its sports bodies argue for the return of its athletes to international sports. In a ruling announced on Oct. 30, the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled the International Ice Hockey Federation's exclusion of Russian athletes from its tournaments unlawful, paving the way for Russia's return to the sport. Belarusian athletes have faced similar bans for Minsk's role in Russia's war. Belarusian dictator Alexander Lukashenko allowed Russia to use the country as a launchpad at the onset of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, with Russian troops advancing toward Kyiv from Belarus in the early days of the war.

Movement for Social Democracy Holds Congress to Launch as a Political Party
articles.summary: Movement for Social Democracy, a progressive force that emerged during ongoing anti-government protests, held an inaugural congress in Tbilisi on November 15 to launch as a political party. The movement, which draws on the social democratic legacy of Georgia’s First Republic (1918–1921) to develop a platform focused on solidarity and social justice, seeks to establish …
articles.body: Movement for Social Democracy, a progressive force that emerged during ongoing anti-government protests, held an inaugural congress in Tbilisi on November 15 to launch as a political party. The movement, which draws on the social democratic legacy of Georgia's First Republic (1918–1921) to develop a platform focused on solidarity and social justice, seeks to establish itself as a political party amid Georgia's prolonged political crisis and an increasingly restrictive environment for political opposition and civil society. During the event at Tbilisi's Courtyard Marriott hotel, which was also livestreamed on social media, the founding members presented the party's charter, elected a 16-member body to govern the party for the coming year, and approved a five-member audit commission and two individuals authorized to represent the party. At least 337 people registered as willing to become party members at the time of the inaugural congress, the group said. “Today's decision to establish a new political party must become an answer to the despair and nihilism prevalent in the country; it must become an opportunity for people who have been driven out of politics, deprived of their voice, impoverished, and oppressed; it must lay the groundwork for restoring meaning to citizenship and bringing citizens themselves back into politics," Sopho Verdzeuli, elected as one of the persons to represent the party, said during the congress. Who’s Who in Georgian Party Politics? A Guide to the Party Landscape in 2026 Movement for Social Democracy emerged through the months of pro-EU, anti-government protests that erupted on November 28, 2024. Many of its members first came together through the daily "Public Broadcaster" rallies and marches, which called for fair coverage by the state television channel. The group gradually evolved into a broader movement embracing social and political causes, formally launching a movement in February 2025. According to the Movement, the establishment as a party comes in response "to a severe political crisis, deepening social and economic inequality, the erosion of democratic institutions, and the country's growing isolation from the European Union - trends that collectively clear the path for the rapid rise of authoritarianism." The group seeks to operate with principles of strong internal democracy and collective decision-making. The movement says that it brings together professionals across various fields, students, emigrants, and others committed to social justice. "We believe that democracy has no future in this country without social justice, just as social justice cannot exist without a democratic political system," Verdzeuli said as he addressed the founding members. According to the party's foundational programme, the movement seeks to address the "unbearable and hopeless" situation in the country with "fundamentally new solutions" rather than retreating "from today's authoritarian dead end to a past in which the principles of liberal democracy and a liberal economic order are presumed to have worked better." 20/07/2026 - Georgian Opposition Braces for New Jail Verdicts Amid Search for Broader Strategy The movement has emerged to fill a longstanding gap in Georgia's party landscape, which, while including a number of liberal, pro-European groups, has long lacked a political force with a strong progressive focus. Despite the widely acknowledged need for new visions to address the country's social and economic problems, and the success of a number of progressive campaigns in recent years, the country's left has until recently struggled to consolidate into a prominent, influential political force. The delay has been attributed to lingering anti-socialist stigmas in post-Soviet society, the difficulties of breaking into a political arena shaped by financial disparities and government crackdown, and the failure of various progressive groups to overcome their differences and unite. The group, however, has yet to complete its official registration as a political party with the Public Registry. Other recently established political forces have reported facing obstacles in the registration process in recent months and years. articles.title: Uzbekistan and CCAC to expand cooperation on methane cuts
articles.summary: Uzbekistan and the Climate and Clean Air Coalition plan joint action on methane, black carbon and other climate pollutants, including a regional air quality initiative.
articles.body: Tashkent, Uzbekistan (UzDaily.uz) — Uzbekistan and the Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC) have agreed to develop a joint plan to reduce methane emissions and other climate pollutants, the National Committee for Ecology and Climate Change said. The agreement was reached at a meeting between Aziz Abdukhakimov, presidential adviser on ecology and chairman of the National Committee for Ecology and Climate Change, and Martina Otto, head of the CCAC Secretariat. The talks took place on the sidelines of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya. The parties discussed expanding cooperation to reduce emissions of methane, black carbon and other short-lived climate pollutants. They also considered joint projects to improve ambient air quality. Uzbekistan joined the Global Methane Pledge in May 2022 and became a state partner of the CCAC in 2024. Two joint projects with a combined value of US$4.6 million are already under way. Uzbekistan also thanked the coalition for including the country in its Super Pollutant Country Action Accelerator programme. The programme provides a US$4 million support package for institutional capacity-building and technical assistance across four priority areas. The parties also discussed a project titled "National Strategy for Reducing Black Carbon Emissions and Improving Air Quality". The project is valued at US$600,000, with implementation scheduled to begin in December 2026. Uzbekistan welcomed new initiatives from the CCAC and the UN Environment Programme (UNEP), including a global economic assessment of measures to address climate change and air pollution. According to an assessment presented at the meeting, every dollar invested could generate approximately US$15 in economic returns. Uzbekistan also expressed interest in the Farmers FIRST initiative, which aims to reduce emissions from agriculture. To improve coordination, the Uzbek side proposed establishing a National Unit for Short-Lived Climate Pollutants under the National Centre for Climate Change. The proposed unit would coordinate the work of relevant ministries and organisations in energy, waste management, transport and agriculture. The participants also discussed joint measures to improve air quality in Central Asia. They highlighted President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's initiative to establish the Clean Air of Central Asia interstate consortium. The consortium is expected to help attract green financing for industrial modernisation and emissions reduction. In this context, Uzbekistan proposed hosting a regional CCAC workshop in Tashkent in 2027. The event would focus on air quality and reducing black carbon and methane emissions. Following the talks, the parties agreed to prepare a joint work plan under the Accelerator programme. The document is expected to include specific activities, implementation deadlines and co-financing mechanisms. The participants confirmed their interest in further developing the partnership and implementing initiatives to reduce climate pollutants in Uzbekistan and Central Asia.
